gaps.area: fx - burst vs stream ids, effect radius, bolts, telegraph kinds
gaps.problem: FxSystem.spawn is a one-shot at a fixed point, but 14 FxIds describe states that last and move with their emitter (lanceCharge, riveterCharge, lancerCharge 1.6 s, bossCharge, bossSweepCharge, bossSweepHit, tickArm, enemySmoke, enemySparks, slideSparks, steamVent, sparkShower, hazardArc, supplyTrail). Nothing says whether one call is the whole effect or one puff, so the fx engineer and every caller will pick opposite answers (one call of a 0.1 s puff = invisible charge; a per-frame call of a 1.6 s effect = 100x overdraw). Size is equally undefined: combat.explode picks explosionSmall/Large by radius but FxSpawnOptions only has a unitless `scale`, so the fireball will not match the damage radius (grenade 6.5 m x grenadePowerMul, hornet 5, tick 5, mortar 4.5, explosive crit 3.5). Also unspecified: which ids draw a sky bolt themselves (bossLightningStrike / spawnFlash / lightningImpact vs fx.lightningBolt), what the six TelegraphKinds look like and their default colour (spawn is lightning-themed but the doc says every default is hazard yellow), and whether quality particleScale may thin gameplay-critical visuals.
gaps.proposedChange: FxSpawnOptions adds `radius?: number` (world radius in metres the effect must visually cover; authored size when omitted; combat.explode ALWAYS passes its damage radius; `scale` stays a cosmetic multiplier) and `charge?: number` (0..1 progress for charge ids). core/constants.ts adds `export const FX_STREAM_IDS: readonly FxId[] = ['lanceCharge','riveterCharge','lancerCharge','bossCharge','bossSweepCharge','bossSweepHit','tickArm','enemySmoke','enemySparks','slideSparks','steamVent','sparkShower','hazardArc','supplyTrail']`. Doc on spawn: 'BURST ids (every id not in FX_STREAM_IDS): one call = the complete effect, self-ending within 2.5 s. STREAM ids: one call = one puff of <= 0.25 s at `position`; the owner calls spawn every 0.05 s of its own clock while the state lasts; fx never sustains or follows them.' 'No FxId draws a bolt: bolts are always fx.lightningBolt; spawnFlash, lightningImpact, bossLightningStrike and chainArc are only the burst at the end point.' TelegraphKind doc: ring = static outline; circle = disc filling to radius; spawn = double ring with rotating ticks, default PALETTE.lightning; strike = disc + cross-hair; mortar = disc + inward chevrons; all but spawn default to PALETTE.hazard. 'particleScale thins secondary particles only: telegraphs, beams, tracers, bolts, damage numbers and the core flash of every explosion are never reduced.'

gaps.area: fx + audio - handle identity (stale handle controls somebody else's effect)
gaps.problem: BeamHandle / TelegraphHandle / TrailHandle / LoopHandle promise 'dead handles ignore every call', while the brief demands pooling with no allocation per spawn. The natural implementation pools the handle objects: lancer A stops its lock laser, the pooled handle is reissued to lancer B, then A's onDespawn calls stop() on its stale reference and kills B's laser (same for telegraph.cancel, trail.detach, loop.stop). The contract neither forbids reuse nor obliges owners to drop references, so both sides will assume the other is safe.
gaps.proposedChange: Doc on all four handle interfaces: 'A handle is bound to ONE effect for the whole session. Implement it as a fresh small object or a {slot, generation} proxy per call; never hand out a handle object that later controls another effect. Any call on a dead handle is a no-op for ever, so owners may keep stale handles.' Add to FxSystem/AudioSystem docs: 'beam(), telegraph(), attachTrail() and loop() may allocate one small handle per call (they are never called per frame); when a pool is exhausted or audio is not running they return one shared frozen dead handle (active === false) and never throw.'

gaps.area: audio + fx - nothing can stop a one-shot; cleanup of effects owned by a dead entity
gaps.problem: play/playAt return void. Long one-shots tied to an attacker (lancerTelegraph ~1.6 s whine, spawnTelegraph 0.8 s, conductorSweepCharge, tickTelegraph, mortarWhistle, sounds queued with `delay`) keep sounding after the attacker died or the attack was cancelled - an audible lie about a threat that no longer exists. Loops, beams, telegraphs and trails rely on every one of 7 independently written enemy kinds (and combat's projectile removal) remembering to stop each handle in onDespawn; one forgotten handle is a permanent hum / floating laser until the next reset.
gaps.proposedChange: `SoundOptions.owner?: number` and `LoopOptions.owner?: number` (entity id: enemy.id, projectile id). `AudioSystem.stopOwner(ownerId: number, fadeSeconds?: number): void` - fades (default 0.06 s) every one-shot, pending delayed one-shot and loop started with that owner. `BeamOptions.owner?: number`, `TelegraphOptions.owner?: number`, `attachTrail(kind: TrailKind, position: THREE.Vector3, color?: number, owner?: number): TrailHandle`, and `FxSystem.cancelOwner(ownerId: number): void` (stops beams, cancels telegraphs, detaches trails of that owner). Contract: the enemy manager calls `ctx.audio.stopOwner(actor.id)` and `ctx.fx.cancelOwner(actor.id)` on every death/despawn before onDespawn; combat does the same with the projectile id when a projectile is removed. Kinds pass `owner: actor.id` on everything positional.

gaps.area: audio lifecycle - loops started in init()/reset() never play; reset cuts the click that caused it
gaps.problem: (1) Before unlock, loop() returns a dead handle, and unlock only happens at the first gesture, so any ambient loop a system starts in init() (world: gateHum, hazardHum, jumpPadHum, steamHiss) is dead for ever. (2) reset order is world -> render -> fx -> audio -> ...; audio.reset() = stopAll() kills every loop, so loops that world/render/fx start in their own reset() die a few lines later in the same resetAll(). By the letter of the contract the world's ambience can never sound. (3) UI plays 'uiConfirm' in the click handler and then calls game.startRun/toMenu, whose resetAll() -> audio.reset() -> stopAll() cuts that click after 0 ms.
gaps.proposedChange: core/game.ts resetAll(): reset `ctx.audio` FIRST, then world, render, fx, combat, player, weapons, enemies, director, ui (update LIFECYCLE ORDER in types.ts: 'reset: audio first, then init order'). AudioSystem doc: 'reset()/stopAll() stop the sfx and ambience buses only - never voices on the UI bus and never the music.' Rule for persistent ambient loops (world, director supplyBeacon): 'acquire lazily in update(): `if (!h.active && ctx.audio.unlocked) h = ctx.audio.loop(id, opts)`; never in init() or reset()'. loop() while not running returns the shared dead handle without allocating.

gaps.area: audio - which time scale drives the global pitch / low-pass
gaps.problem: Audio 'follows ctx.time.scale with a global SFX pitch/low-pass'. ctx.time.scale is the minimum of ALL requests, including hitstop (0.05 for 50-250 ms on heavy hits) and the perk-select freeze (0). Following it literally produces a violent pitch dive to 5 % on every hit-stop and a dive to zero when the perk screen opens; the mapping from scale to pitch is not given either (0.4 world speed must not become 0.4 pitch = 1.3 octaves down).
gaps.proposedChange: AudioSystem doc: 'the slow-motion treatment follows `s = Math.min(ctx.time.getScale("overclock"), ctx.time.getScale("slowmo"))` only - never hitstop, perkSelect or debug. pitchMul = clamp(1 - 0.5 * (1 - s), 0.7, 1) (0.4 -> 0.7); low-pass cutoff = lerp(20000, 2200, clamp((1 - s) / 0.6, 0, 1)) Hz; both approached with setTargetAtTime, time constant 0.09 s. Applied only to voices that are time-scaled (positional world sounds); music gets the low-pass at half depth and no pitch change.'

gaps.area: render vs fx vs audio - ambient storm has two owners
gaps.problem: types.ts (FxSystem.setWeather) says storm weathers own ambient lightning: fx picks the moments, draws distant bolts, calls render.lightningFlash and plays thunderFar/thunderNear. assign/render.md tells the render engineer to do 'random lightning during stormnight/eclipse ... and thunder through the audio system after a distance delay'. Both will ship it: double flashes and double thunder. Same split for the eclipse vortex (render sky 'vortex above the Core Spire' vs WeatherId 'vortex') and for wind (audio 'storm wind bed' vs fx one-shots windGust/staticCrackle). fx.md also says fx must tame flashes for reduceFlashes while SettingsData says only render does.
gaps.proposedChange: Contract text: 'RENDER never schedules lightning and never plays a sound. FX weather schedules strikes at rate TIME_OF_DAY[render.timeOfDay].lightningPerMinute * render.lighting.storm; one strike = optional fx.lightningBolt 150-400 m away + ctx.render.lightningFlash(intensity, dir) + ctx.audio.play(distance < 200 ? "thunderNear" : "thunderFar", { delay: distance / 343 }).' 'render.lightningFlash boosts sun + hemisphere intensity for 0.25 s with 2-3 flickers, glows the sky shader toward `direction`, adds a post flash <= 0.35 (<= 0.1 with reduceFlashes) and never changes the light count.' 'Vortex: the sky vortex (render) is centred above ctx.world.bossArena.center; fx weather "vortex" only adds near-camera streaks.' 'AUDIO owns the continuous beds (wind, static-rain hiss) from timeOfDay:changed + render.lighting.storm; FX plays only the one-shots thunderNear, thunderFar, lightningCrack, staticCrackle, windGust.' 'reduceFlashes: render caps post flash + lightning; fx halves lightFlash intensity and disables bolt strobing; nobody else checks it.' Add `LightingState.flash: number` (0..1 current lightning boost) so fx/world can flicker in sync.

gaps.area: rendering conventions - custom shaders, colour space, runtime recompiles
gaps.problem: RENDERING CONVENTIONS covers standard materials only. World (gate barrier, slag), fx (particles, beams, telegraphs), enemies (shields), weapons (readouts) and render (sky) will all write ShaderMaterial / onBeforeCompile code. types.ts says the frame is rendered in HDR and tone-mapped by render, but assign/render.md says 'Low preset: no composer'. With a direct-to-canvas path three.js applies tone mapping and sRGB inside each material, which custom shaders only get if they include the tonemapping/colorspace chunks; with the HDR target path those chunks must be absent. Each engineer will guess, and effects will look different per preset. Also missing: fog for custom world shaders, colour space of canvas textures, and the list of runtime changes that recompile every program (the brief only mentions light count).
gaps.proposedChange: Add to RENDERING CONVENTIONS: '- Render draws BOTH scenes into a linear HDR target (HalfFloat, RGBA8 fallback) on EVERY preset including low; renderer.toneMapping stays NoToneMapping and tone mapping + sRGB happen only in render's final pass (overrides assign/render.md "no composer"). Custom fragment shaders therefore output LINEAR scene-referred colour and must NOT include tonemapping_fragment / colorspace_fragment. - World-space custom shaders set `fog: true`, merge THREE.UniformsLib.fog and include fog_pars_vertex / fog_vertex / fog_pars_fragment / fog_fragment. - Hex colours reach uniforms/attributes only through `new THREE.Color(hex)` (sRGB -> linear). onBeforeCompile users set customProgramCacheKey. - Canvas albedo/emissive textures: `colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace`; normal/roughness/data maps: NoColorSpace; anisotropy 4; all textures are created in init(). - After init() never set material.needsUpdate, never add/remove a map, never toggle flatShading / vertexColors / alphaTest / transparent, never toggle light.visible or light.castShadow, never switch scene.fog or scene.environment between null and a value: each recompiles programs. Animate uniforms and numeric material properties only. - Materials are never shared between ctx.scene and ctx.viewScene.'

gaps.area: rendering conventions - draw order of transparent objects across systems
gaps.problem: Five systems add transparent objects to ctx.scene: world (energy gates, glass, slag glow), enemies (bulwark/boss shields), director (pickup glow), fx (decals, telegraphs, smoke, additive particles, beams, weather, damage numbers) and render (sky). three.js sorts transparents by the depth of the OBJECT origin; fx batches are single instanced meshes with their origin at 0,0,0, so the whole particle system sorts as one object against a gate or a shield and pops in front of / behind it depending on where the camera stands. With no shared renderOrder table each team picks its own numbers.
gaps.proposedChange: core/constants.ts: `export const RENDER_ORDER = { SKY: -100, OPAQUE: 0, DECAL: 10, TELEGRAPH: 12, WORLD_TRANSPARENT: 20, PICKUP: 25, ENEMY_SHIELD: 30, FX_ALPHA: 40, BEAM: 50, FX_ADDITIVE: 60, WEATHER: 70, DAMAGE_NUMBER: 80 } as const;`. Convention: 'every transparent or additive material sets depthWrite:false and its mesh sets renderOrder from RENDER_ORDER; decals/telegraphs also use polygonOffset(-2,-2); batched meshes set frustumCulled = false; the sky uses depthTest:false + SKY and is excluded from fog.'

gaps.area: render + settings - automatic quality, dynamic governor, shader recompiles
gaps.problem: assign/render.md asks for a 'sensible automatic default from the device', but SettingsData.quality is a plain preset defaulting to 'high' (DPR 1.5, 2048 shadows) for phones and iGPUs alike; if render writes a detected preset into settings it is persisted and can no longer be told apart from a user choice. The 'quality:changed' doc says it is also emitted 'by the dynamic quality governor': a governor that flips shadows or bloom recompiles every material at exactly the moment the frame rate is already bad, and FX would re-read caps (or reallocate) mid-fight. Nothing says what the governor measures, and with manual stepping (?test=1, SwiftShader) it would drop to 0.5 and blur every harness screenshot.
gaps.proposedChange: `export type QualitySetting = QualityPreset | 'auto';` `SettingsData.quality: QualitySetting` (DEFAULT_SETTINGS.quality = 'auto'; settings.ts sanitize accepts it). `RenderSystem.quality: QualityPreset` stays the RESOLVED preset; add `readonly qualityIsAuto: boolean`. Render resolves 'auto' once in init(): `(pointer: coarse)` -> 'low' when min(screen.width, screen.height) < 800 else 'medium'; desktop with UNMASKED_RENDERER matching /SwiftShader|llvmpipe|Intel|Iris|UHD|Mali|Adreno|PowerVR/ -> 'medium'; else 'high'. 'quality:changed' doc: 'emitted only by setQuality (preset change) - NEVER by the resolution governor.' Governor contract: changes only resolutionScale (0.5..1, steps <= 0.1, >= 1 s apart, hysteresis 52/58 fps), measures ctx.time.realDt, ignores frames >= 0.1 s and the first 2 s after a mode change or resize, is OFF when ctx.testMode or !settings.dynamicResolution, never touches shadows/bloom/particle caps, and scales by rendering into a viewport of fixed-size targets (no reallocation per step).

gaps.area: fx - light pool units and moving lights
gaps.problem: lightFlash(position, color, intensity, radius, seconds) takes intensity 'in candela-ish three.js units'. Weapons, combat, 7 enemy kinds, director and world all call it blind; with physically based falloff one engineer will pass 2 and another 2000. There is also no way to keep a light on a moving thing (rocket in flight, charging lancer, boss core): calling lightFlash every frame takes a new slot each call ('when all 6 are busy the weakest is stolen'), so one rocket eats the whole pool in 6 frames. render.muzzleFlash(color, intensity) has no unit at all.
gaps.proposedChange: `lightFlash(position: Vec3Like, color: number, intensity: number, radius: number, seconds: number, key?: number): void;` Doc: 'intensity is NORMALISED: 1 = rifle muzzle flash, 2 = rocket/plasma impact, 3 = grenade, 6 = boss burst (clamped to 8); fx converts to three.js units so that 1 lights a white wall 3 m away to about mid-grey. `key` (non-zero entity id): a call whose key already holds a slot refreshes that slot (position, intensity, timer) instead of taking a new one - the ONLY way to make a moving or pulsing light; un-keyed per-frame calls are forbidden. At most 2 slots may be held by keyed lights.' Add `readonly activeLights: number`. `render.muzzleFlash(color: number, intensity: number)`: 'intensity 0..1 normalised, decays in 60 ms'.

gaps.area: render / fx / audio - time of day and weather after reset and at boot
gaps.problem: setTimeOfDay emits 'timeOfDay:changed' only on a change, and FX (weather) and audio (ambience) are told to follow that event. At boot render.init() runs before fx/audio subscribe, and the first wave asks for 'dusk' while already at dusk, so no event ever reaches them: no embers, no wind bed. After a run that ended in Eclipse, toMenu() resets everything but the RenderSystem doc does not say reset() returns to dusk (the stub does), and fx.reset() = clear() is undefined for weather: either the menu sits in Eclipse, or render snaps to dusk and fx.reset (which runs after render.reset) wipes the weather it just switched to.
gaps.proposedChange: RenderSystem doc: 'reset(): post defaults, cancel lightning, setTimeOfDay("dusk", 0). setTimeOfDay emits timeOfDay:changed only when the TARGET id changes; called mid-blend it starts from the current blended state; the blend runs on realDt (continues while paused / during the perk freeze).' FxSystem + AudioSystem doc: 'never rely on the event for the initial state: in init() AND at the end of reset() sync from ctx.render.timeOfDay (fx: setWeather(TIME_OF_DAY[ctx.render.timeOfDay].weather)). clear() removes particles, decals, beams, telegraphs, trails and damage numbers but keeps the weather id and its particles.' Director: debugSkipToWave calls setTimeOfDay(id, 0).

gaps.area: world + player - jump pads
gaps.problem: JumpPadInfo carries position, velocity and zone only. The world engineer solves `velocity` for a ballistic arc (channel crossing, terrace hop), but player.launch only promises 'replace the velocity, leaves the ground'. A normal controller clamps horizontal air speed to walk/sprint speed and applies air drag/air control, so a pad that needs 12 m/s horizontally lands the player in the slag. There is no trigger radius (world test, minimap icon, bot), no landing point and no id.
gaps.proposedChange: `export interface JumpPadInfo { readonly id: number; readonly position: THREE.Vector3; /** Trigger radius in metres. */ readonly radius: number; /** Launch velocity solved for PLAYER.GRAVITY with zero air control. */ readonly velocity: THREE.Vector3; /** Feet position where that arc lands. */ readonly target: THREE.Vector3; readonly zone: ZoneId; }`. PlayerSystem.launch doc: 'non-additive launch: until the next landing the player keeps the launched horizontal velocity - no air-speed clamp, no air drag; air control may change it by at most 3 m/s in total; gravity is exactly PLAYER.GRAVITY; a dash or double jump ends the guarantee; no fall damage on that landing.' World doc: 'a pad fires when the grounded player feet are within `radius`, re-arms after 0.5 s, never launches enemies; world validates in its vitest that every arc clears geometry and ends on a walkable cell.'

gaps.area: world - rules that other systems silently depend on
gaps.problem: Several world rules are missing or contradicted by assign/world.md: (1) world.update also runs in menu/gameover/victory and during the death delay, but nothing says hazards, jump pads and the fall-out rule stop there. (2) Hazards damage 'through the player interface' only, so an enemy knocked into the slag channel (nav-blocked) becomes an unreachable straggler; hazard volumes are not exposed. (3) world.md asks for 4 m wall bands between zones: with zone AABBs that stop at the walls, zoneAt()/EnemyHandle.zone are null inside every gate corridor. (4) groundHeightAt has no stated mask: searched from the top of the world it returns the top of the invisible perimeter clip (y = 40) or of a closed gate. (5) world.md makes pipe racks 'visual only, >= 4 m up' while wasps fly at 4-9 m and grenades arc there: they pass through visible geometry. (6) reset() goes through setGateOpen, which plays the close animation, fx and sound on every run start. (7) two gates per boundary need distinct ids but the doc examples are one id per boundary.
gaps.proposedChange: WorldSystem doc: 'update(): animation in every simulated mode; gameplay rules (hazard damage, jump pads, gate-denied, fall-out) only while ctx.game.mode === "playing" && ctx.player.alive.' Add `readonly hazards: readonly HazardInfo[]` with `export interface HazardInfo { readonly aabb: Readonly<Aabb>; readonly kind: 'slag' | 'steam' | 'arc'; readonly dps: number; readonly active: boolean; }` and 'every 0.25 s of scaled time world calls combat.applyDamage (type "hazard", faction "neutral", weapon "world", dir 0) on the player AND on every live enemy whose position is inside an active hazard'. 'ZoneInfo.aabb tile world.bounds along X with no gaps (boundary = middle of the wall band): zoneAt never returns null inside bounds.' 'groundHeightAt only considers boxes with BOTH COL.PLAYER and COL.PROJECTILE whose tag does not start with "gate:".' 'Everything below y = 16 m inside the perimeter that is visible is collidable (at least COL.ENEMY | COL.PROJECTILE); visual-only dressing lives above 16 m or outside the walls.' `setGateOpen(id: string, open: boolean, instant?: boolean): void` - reset() uses instant (no animation, fx or sound; still emits gate:state). Gate ids: `<from>-<to>:main` / `<from>-<to>:side`.

gaps.area: ui + input - keyboard / gamepad navigation activates twice
gaps.problem: Enter is bound to 'uiConfirm' and arrows to 'uiLeft/Right/Up/Down' in input.ts, and outside gameplay the keydown is NOT prevented when a button or slider has focus, so the browser also performs the native action. A UI that reacts to justPressed('uiConfirm') (needed for the gamepad A button) fires every focused button twice on Enter (startRun twice, a toggle flipping back), and a range input moves two steps per arrow press. Who moves focus, whether a screen auto-focuses a control and how sticks repeat is unspecified. The CONTROLS screen also cannot list both columns because bindingLabel only answers for the current device.
gaps.proposedChange: UiSystem doc: 'Focus model: every screen has exactly one focused control (focus the primary control on open, restore the previous one on close). uiUp/Down/Left/Right move DOM focus; the UI implements repeat itself (0.4 s, then every 0.12 s). Activation and value changes: keyboard and mouse use the NATIVE behaviour of the focused element only; the UI reacts to justPressed("uiConfirm") (-> document.activeElement.click()) and to uiLeft/uiRight value steps ONLY while ctx.input.device === "gamepad". Every button action lives in its DOM click handler. A screen ignores confirm for 0.3 s after it opens.' `Input.bindingLabel(action: InputAction, device?: InputDevice): string` (default: current device).

gaps.area: core/input.ts - pointer lock is disabled for good after gamepad or non-gesture starts
gaps.problem: tryLock() (input.ts 299-312) runs for every requestCapture(), including runs started with a gamepad button or from a frame callback, where the browser has no user activation and rejects the request. onLockFailed() (290-297) counts each rejection while everLocked is false and sets lockDisabled = true after MAX_LOCK_FAILURES; nothing ever clears it. Start with a pad, pick one perk (release + re-request), and a player who then takes the mouse is stuck in free-look for the rest of the page life. Combined with the double count already reported it takes two attempts.
gaps.proposedChange: input.ts: `const tryLock = (fromGesture: boolean): void => { if (lockDisabled || locked || !wantsCapture || device !== 'keyboardMouse') return; ... const counted = fromGesture || navigator.userActivation?.isActive === true; ... on rejection: if (counted) onLockFailed(); else refreshLookMode(); }`. requestCapture() calls tryLock(false); onMouseDown calls tryLock(true). When the device changes to 'keyboardMouse' while wantsCapture && !locked, the next canvas mousedown retries. Reset `lockFailures = 0` whenever a request was not counted.

gaps.area: core/input.ts - gamepads with non-standard mapping or resting axes
gaps.problem: pollGamepad() accepts any connected device with >= 10 buttons (input.ts 496-503) without checking `mapping === 'standard'`, and marks the pad 'active' by LEVEL (stick magnitude > 0.5, lines 533-534). Wheels, flight sticks, pedals and some receivers report a resting axis at -1 or 1: the player drifts or spins for ever, and setDevice('gamepad') fires every frame, fighting setDevice('keyboardMouse') from each key press - 'input:device' ping-pongs every frame (UI rebuilds its prompts), and mouse movement of <= 2 px per event is dropped while device is 'gamepad' (line 420), so fine aim stutters.
gaps.proposedChange: input.ts: skip pads whose `mapping !== 'standard'`. Keep `axisArmed[4]` flags: an axis contributes only after it has been seen with |value| < 0.25 once. Switch device to 'gamepad' on EDGES only: a button newly pressed this poll, or a stick magnitude crossing 0.5 upward; never from a held level. Unit-test with a fake pad whose axes rest at (1, -1).

gaps.area: core/input.ts - wheel on trackpads
gaps.problem: onWheel (input.ts 434-440) latches weaponNext/weaponPrev for every wheel event with deltaY != 0. A trackpad two-finger scroll or a free-spinning wheel emits dozens of small events over about a second (plus inertia), so the weapon cycles on every frame of the gesture. The brief's target machine is a laptop.
gaps.proposedChange: input.ts: `let wheelAccum = 0, lastWheelStep = -Infinity, lastWheelEvent = -Infinity;` in onWheel: `const t = nowMs(); if (t - lastWheelEvent > 250) wheelAccum = 0; lastWheelEvent = t; wheelAccum += e.deltaY * (e.deltaMode === 1 ? 40 : e.deltaMode === 2 ? 400 : 1); if (Math.abs(wheelAccum) >= 80 && t - lastWheelStep >= 140) { latchPressed[ACTION_INDEX[wheelAccum > 0 ? 'weaponNext' : 'weaponPrev']] = 1; wheelAccum = 0; lastWheelStep = t; }`.

gaps.area: core/game.ts - error containment for presentation systems
gaps.problem: (1) ok(key) is only called from update(), late() and draw() (game.ts 163-180, 354-362). For every other contained call - onModeChange:*, reset:*, unlock:audio, startRun:director, resize:render, wantsPointer:ui, update:bot - the streak is never cleared, so '3 in a row' really means '3 times ever': a reset:fx that throws once in each of three runs raises the fatal panel. (2) unlockAudio() is called on EVERY pointerdown/keydown (430-432, 462-463); if AudioContext creation throws on a device, three clicks kill the game. (3) More generally a WebAudio or particle exception should cost sound or sparks, not the run, yet update:audio / update:fx escalate to fatal like gameplay, and gameplay systems call ctx.audio.* / ctx.fx.* inside their own updates, so an fx bug surfaces as 'update:weapons' failing.
gaps.proposedChange: game.ts: `const guarded = (key: string, fn: () => void): void => { try { fn(); ok(key); } catch (error) { contain(key, error); } };` used for onModeChange, reset, unlock, startRun:director, resize and the bot; call ok() after successful wantsPointer/consumesPauseAction. `const NEVER_FATAL = new Set(['unlock:audio','update:audio','reset:audio','update:fx','lateUpdate:fx','reset:fx','update:bot','resize:render']);` - for these, after 3 failures core stops calling that method, reports once and carries on. Contract for AudioSystem and FxSystem: 'every public non-lifecycle method is wrapped at the boundary and never throws: on an internal exception call ctx.game.reportError("audio" | "fx", error) once and switch the system to its null behaviour (no-ops, shared dead handle).'

gaps.area: tools + src/main.ts - the sandboxed, query-less embedding cannot be tested
gaps.problem: The harness always loads `/?test=1` at top level. The shipped form is an inline page in a sandboxed frame with no query string, where main.ts isTestMode() can never be true, so manual stepping is unavailable exactly where pointer lock, fullscreen and storage are denied. Verified with a probe against dist: inside `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` localStorage throws SecurityError, requestPointerLock rejects with SecurityError and logs a console error, document.fullscreenEnabled is false, window.name set by the host IS readable - and the game does not load at all, because assets/game.js is fetched as a module from an opaque origin and the dist server sends no CORS header (only the inline 'game files could not be loaded' panel appears). input.ts also hard-disables lock, edge-turn and blur handling in test mode, so those paths are never executed by any tool.
gaps.proposedChange: src/main.ts isTestMode(): `return new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('test') === '1' || window.name === 'sh-test';`. tools/harness.mjs: `launchGame({ mode, port, width, height, touch, query, test = true, embed = 'none' | 'sandbox', dpr = 1, args = [], reducedMotion = 'reduce' })`; embed 'sandbox' serves a host page containing `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" name="sh-test" src="/index.html">`, adds `access-control-allow-origin: *` to the dist server, runs `sh()` inside that Frame and ignores exactly the two expected console errors ('Blocked pointer lock on an element because the element's frame is sandboxed', 'Permissions policy violation: fullscreen'). smoke.mjs gains `--embed sandbox`: boots; `SH.ctx.storage.persistent === false`; a run starts; lookMode 'free'; page.mouse.move over the canvas turns the view; ArrowLeft turns the view; no fatal. `test: false` runs the real rAF loop for auto-pause, dynamic-resolution and pointer-policy checks.

gaps.area: index.html - the optional web font can block boot
gaps.problem: index.html 15-20 loads Google Fonts with a plain `<link rel="stylesheet">` in <head>. That is render-blocking and script-blocking: neither the boot screen nor the module script runs until the request completes or fails. Where fonts.googleapis.com is black-holed (corporate proxies, some regions, flaky mobile) the page stays blank for the full connection timeout. The harness hides this by fulfilling the request instantly. This breaks 'boots instantly' and 'must degrade to a system fallback stack'.
gaps.proposedChange: Replace the stylesheet link with a non-blocking load: `<link rel="preload" as="style" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...&display=swap" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'" onerror="this.remove()">` (keep the two preconnects). Add `-webkit-touch-callout: none;` to the body rule (long-press on a held touch button opens the iOS callout). UI rule: 'never wait for document.fonts; all text metrics must hold with the fallback stacks.'

gaps.area: fx - clock of the player's own effects during Overclock
gaps.problem: fx.update runs on scaled world time. During Overclock (0.4) the player 'shoots at full speed', but the muzzle flashes, tracers, casings and rail beam they spawn play at 0.4x: a 50 ms muzzle flash lasts 125 ms and overlaps the next shot at 720 rpm into a constant glow, and a tracer needs 0.23 s to cross 30 m while the hitscan damage landed instantly. The gameplay review fixed this for projectiles (ProjectileOptions.clock) but fx has no equivalent.
gaps.proposedChange: `FxSpawnOptions.clock?: 'world' | 'player'`, `TracerOptions.clock?: 'world' | 'player'`, `BeamOptions.clock?: 'world' | 'player'` (default 'world'). FxSystem doc: 'update(dt) advances world-clock effects with dt and player-clock effects with ctx.time.unscaledDt while ctx.game.mode === "playing" (with dt in every other mode, so nothing freezes after the run ends).' Weapons pass clock 'player' for muzzle*, casing*, lanceDischarge, hornetBackblast, meleeSwing, their tracers and the rail beam; impact sparks, decals and damage numbers stay on the world clock.

gaps.area: world + fx - decals on stair-stepped ramps, gates and glass
gaps.problem: Ramps are smooth visuals over 0.25 m stair-step collision. Hitscan and projectile impacts report the step box: axis-aligned normals and points up to 0.25 m off the visible slope, so bullet holes and scorch marks float above or sink into ramps as horizontal quads. Decals on a closed energy gate stay hanging in the doorway after the gate opens. fx.decal gets neither the box nor the surface, so only callers could filter, and nothing tells them to.
gaps.proposedChange: `BoxDesc.decals?: boolean` (default true) and `CollisionBox.decals: boolean`; world sets false on ramp step boxes, gate boxes and glass. `FxSystem.decal(kind: DecalKind, position: Vec3Like, normal: Vec3Like, size?: number, boxId?: number): void` - fx ignores the call when `ctx.collision.boxes[boxId].decals === false` and drops live decals whose box becomes disabled. Weapons/combat always pass hit.boxId; impact particles are spawned regardless.

gaps.area: render - screen flash has many writers; no shield-hit flash
gaps.problem: post.flash / post.flashColor are raw fields written by combat (explosions), enemies and boss (lightning, white-out) and fx. Writers are told to use `flash = Math.max(flash, v)` but flashColor is a single slot: a weak orange blast can recolour a strong white-violet lightning flash in the same frame. damageFlash is a red vignette only, so shield hits and health hits look identical on screen unless the player abuses the full-screen `flash`.
gaps.proposedChange: `RenderSystem.screenFlash(color: number, intensity: number): void` - strongest wins: `if (intensity > post.flash) { post.flash = intensity; post.flashColor = color; }`; doc post.flash/flashColor as 'written through screenFlash only'. `PostFxParams.shieldFlash: number` ('IMPULSE 0..1 - cyan edge flash when the shield absorbs a hit. Writer: player'). Doc: 'render reads `post` inside render() (draw time), so a value set by a test without stepping is visible to __SH.renderFrame().'

gaps.area: render + world - cinematic cameras
gaps.problem: Only the menu path is described ('render interpolates and loops'). The interpolation is not fixed, so the world engineer cannot guarantee the camera never cuts through geometry (a Catmull-Rom overshoot between safe keys clips a tank). CinematicShot has no FOV and no way to author separate shots. Game-over ('pull-back from where the player fell') and victory ('orbit of the Spire') have no defined focus, and render may not subscribe to boss:defeated. While __SH.setCamera is active, render.update still writes the cinematic camera between core's two overrides, so ui/audio read a different camera than the one drawn.
gaps.proposedChange: `export interface CinematicShot { readonly position: THREE.Vector3; readonly target: THREE.Vector3; readonly seconds: number; /** Vertical FOV in degrees (default 55). */ readonly fov?: number; /** true: hard cut to the next key instead of travelling to it. */ readonly cut?: boolean; }`. Doc: 'render interpolates position and target with centripetal Catmull-Rom over the closed loop (linear time per segment); world guarantees a 1 m radius tube along that curve is free of geometry; the path restarts at key 0 on every entry to the menu.' 'gameover: from the camera pose at the mode change ease over 2.5 s to 7 m behind and 4 m above ctx.player.position (pulled in by collision.raycast with COL.SIGHT), then orbit at 0.1 rad/s looking at player.position + (0,1,0). victory: orbit world.bossArena.center at radius bossArena.radius * 1.25, height hoverHeight * 0.8, 0.12 rad/s.' 'Render writes ctx.camera only when mode is menu/gameover/victory AND !ctx.debug.freeCamera, and calls updateProjectionMatrix after changing fov.'

gaps.area: world + ui - minimap data
gaps.problem: MinimapRect.kind 'pad' does not say drop pad or jump pad, rects carry no height so the 0 / 1.5 / 3 m terraces and ramps cannot be shaded, draw order is undefined (a floor listed after a wall hides it), and the orientation convention for the rotating radar is left to the UI engineer.
gaps.proposedChange: `kind: 'floor' | 'ramp' | 'wall' | 'cover' | 'gate' | 'dropPad' | 'jumpPad' | 'hazard'` and `readonly level: number` (top height in metres). MinimapData doc: 'rects are listed in draw order (floor, ramp, hazard, pads, cover, wall, gate), at most 400. Convention: at yaw 0 north (-Z) is up and +X is right; the radar rotates by player.yaw; gates use world.gates for live state.'

gaps.area: ui - things two systems would both draw, and banner policy
gaps.problem: (1) render.post owns damage vignette, low-health pulse, Overclock treatment, dash blur and ADS vignette, but assign/ui.md also lists low-health and Overclock states; a UI engineer will add CSS vignettes on top. (2) 'score:changed' carries a world position but nobody is assigned the floating '+150' (fx.damageNumber or UI). (3) multikill callouts and FLAWLESS can arrive both as their own events and as 'announce'. (4) Whether banners queue or replace is unstated; the director paces its phases on one assumption, the UI may implement the other. (5) assign/ui.md lists a fatal-error panel that the contract forbids the UI to build. (6) Pause during perk select is undefined.
gaps.proposedChange: UiSystem doc: 'UI draws no full-screen tint, vignette or blur for damage, low health, Overclock, dash or ADS (render.post owns them) and never uses CSS backdrop-filter over the canvas (full-resolution readback every frame). Its only full-screen layers: scope mask, menu scrims, rotate-device nudge. Floating score popups at score:changed.position are UI (DOM pool + render.worldToScreen); fx.damageNumber is damage only. Multikill callouts come from the multikill event (callout line, not a banner); FLAWLESS and every other banner arrive only through announce. Banners: the newest replaces the current one after it has been visible for 0.5 s; no queue. The fatal panel is index.html + core only. Pause is allowed during perk select: the pause menu covers the cards, which return on resume; wantsPointer() stays true.'

gaps.area: core/input.ts - arrow keys on a focused control scroll the host page
gaps.problem: onKeyDown (input.ts 365) prevents the default of Space/arrow keys only when the target is NOT interactive. With a menu button focused (the normal state once the UI drives focus) arrow keys keep their default scroll action. Verified in a sandboxed frame inside a tall host page: five ArrowDown presses with a focused button scrolled the HOST page by 200 px while the game received the keys.
gaps.proposedChange: input.ts onKeyDown: `const t = e.target; const nativeArrows = t instanceof HTMLInputElement || t instanceof HTMLSelectElement || t instanceof HTMLTextAreaElement || (t instanceof HTMLElement && t.getAttribute('role') === 'slider'); if (wantsCapture || (e.code.startsWith('Arrow') && !nativeArrows) || (e.code === 'Space' && !isInteractive(t))) e.preventDefault();`

gaps.area: audio - unlock, suspended contexts, tab visibility
gaps.problem: `unlocked` only says unlock() was called. A context created outside a qualifying gesture stays 'suspended' (verified: 'suspended' in a frame without activation; iOS Safari grants audio activation on touchend/click, not on the pointerdown core listens to; a gamepad-started run has no activation). With currentTime frozen, every play() schedules nodes that never end: the voice cap fills and the backlog bursts on the next resume. Nothing handles a hidden tab: rAF stops, audio.update stops, the look-ahead sequencer starves while the context keeps running. 'Nothing may create an AudioContext before unlock' leaves OfflineAudioContext pre-rendering in doubt.
gaps.proposedChange: AudioSystem doc: 'unlock(): create the context on the first call; on EVERY call `if (ac.state !== "running") void ac.resume().catch(() => {})`. `unlocked` === (context exists && state === "running"). While not running, play/playAt/loop are no-ops (shared dead handle) and nothing is scheduled. Audio owns a visibilitychange listener: hidden -> ac.suspend(); visible -> ac.resume() if it was running. OfflineAudioContext may be used at any time, including init() (buffer pre-rendering needs no gesture).' core/game.ts: register onFirstGesture for 'pointerup', 'touchend' and 'click' as well as pointerdown/keydown.

gaps.area: tools + ui + fx - deterministic visuals under manual stepping
gaps.problem: In ?test=1 the simulation advances only through step(), but CSS transitions/animations and setTimeout run on wall-clock time: a banner or perk card with a 200 ms transition is captured mid-fade or not at all depending on how fast SwiftShader stepped, so UI screenshots are flaky. FX/weather cosmetics may use Math.random and storm weathers fire ambient lightning at random, so two runs of shots.mjs differ and a white flash can land in any frame. The harness has no real touch input (touchTour only calls notifyDevice), no device-pixel-ratio option, and never loads the real fonts.
gaps.proposedChange: `GameContext.cosmeticRng: Rng` (fixed seed in test mode, never reseeded by a run); rule: 'presentation code uses ctx.cosmeticRng, never Math.random'. UiSystem doc: 'everything with a lifetime (banners, hitmarkers, damage arcs, feed entries, callouts, count-ups) is timed by update(realDt), never by animationend / setTimeout; in ctx.testMode the UI adds class `sh-test` to uiRoot, which sets all transition/animation durations to 0s.' FX: 'ambient lightning is suppressed while ctx.testMode unless setWeather was called explicitly'. harness: newContext({ reducedMotion: 'reduce', deviceScaleFactor: dpr }); touchTour performs real `page.touchscreen.tap` on the fire and pause buttons and a drag on the look zone, then asserts mag decreased / yaw changed / mode paused.

gaps.area: debug / test API - presentation systems
gaps.problem: window.__SH cannot put the UI into a named screen (settings, controls, difficulty) or report which screen and focus are active; nothing measures audio (only voiceCount), so 'no clipping with 30 voices' and 'every SoundId is audible' are unverifiable outside the audio engineer's private tool; RenderStats has no program count, so 'no shader compiles during play' cannot be asserted; drawCalls is one total that includes the shadow and post passes, so the per-system budgets (world 150, fx 25, viewmodel 12) cannot be checked; leaks across restarts are invisible because geometries/textures are not in DebugState.
gaps.proposedChange: `export type UiScreen = 'none' | 'menu' | 'difficulty' | 'settings' | 'controls' | 'hud' | 'perkSelect' | 'pause' | 'gameover' | 'victory';` `UiSystem.readonly screen: UiScreen; debugShow(screen: UiScreen | null): void;`. `export interface AudioMeter { state: 'locked' | 'suspended' | 'running'; peak: number; rms: number; clipped: number; voices: number; loops: number; buffersReady: number; buffersTotal: number; }` `AudioSystem.readonly meter: Readonly<AudioMeter>; measure(id: SoundId | LoopId): Promise<{ seconds: number; peak: number; rms: number }>;` (offline render). `RenderStats.programs: number; shadowCalls: number; postCalls: number; resolutionScale: number;`. `FxSystem.readonly stats: Readonly<{ particles: number; decals: number; beams: number; telegraphs: number; trails: number; lights: number; batches: number }>`. Convention: 'each system adds exactly ONE root Object3D named after itself (world, sky, fx, combat, enemies, pickups; weapons in viewScene)' plus `DebugApi.budget(): Record<string, { visibleMeshes: number; triangles: number }>`, `DebugApi.ui(screen: UiScreen | null): void`, `DebugApi.fx(id: FxId, x: number, y: number, z: number): void`, `DebugApi.sound(id: SoundId): void`. DebugState adds geometries, textures, programs, resolutionScale, weather, musicState, musicIntensity, audioState, uiScreen. smoke.mjs asserts programs, geometries and textures are unchanged across the two restarts.

gaps.area: core/game.ts + loop - boot screen never updates; zero dt; boot:progress
gaps.problem: boot() (game.ts 434-456) calls setBootProgress and then awaits each init, but awaiting a synchronous init only yields a microtask: the browser never paints between systems, so the bar sits at its initial 4 % for the whole boot and then jumps. The 'boot:progress' event is useless to the UI, which initialises last and subscribes after every earlier emission. Separately, manual mode and step(0) call frame(0), so every system receives update(0); the contract never says dt can be 0 and a `/ dt` anywhere puts NaN into a transform.
gaps.proposedChange: game.ts boot(): after setBootProgress add `await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));` (setTimeout, not rAF, so hidden tabs and manual mode still boot). Delete 'boot:progress' from EventMap (the #boot element in index.html is the boot screen; UI only fades its menu in on the first game:mode 'menu'). System.update doc: 'dt may be exactly 0 (manual frame(0), step(0), hard freeze): never divide by dt.'

gaps.area: core/game.ts - resize clears the canvas after the frame was drawn
gaps.problem: resize() (game.ts 414-422) runs directly inside the ResizeObserver / window resize callback and calls render.resize(), which reallocates the drawing buffer. ResizeObserver callbacks are delivered after the frame's requestAnimationFrame callbacks and before paint, so the frame just rendered is wiped and a blank frame is presented on every step of a window drag, orientation change or DPR change (visible flicker; composer targets are reallocated on every step as well).
gaps.proposedChange: game.ts: `let resizePending = true; const requestResize = (): void => { resizePending = true; };` registered for both the observer and window resize; at the top of frame() and of renderOnly(): `if (resizePending) { resizePending = false; applyResize(); }` where applyResize is today's resize() body. RenderSystem.resize doc: 'only core calls it, at the start of a frame; a 0x0 canvas is clamped to 1x1.'

gaps.area: fx - camera timing and cost under sub-stepping
gaps.problem: fx.update runs inside the substep loop, before the player's lateUpdate rewrites the camera (recoil, shake), before render.update moves the cinematic camera, and before core applies the free-camera override. Anything fx derives from ctx.camera on the CPU (billboard orientation, the near-camera weather volume, damage-number facing) is one step stale, and wrong for every __SH.setCamera screenshot. Below 30 fps core runs up to 3 substeps per frame; an fx that uploads its instance buffers in update() uploads 3x per frame exactly when the machine is struggling, and a system cannot tell which substep is the last.
gaps.proposedChange: FxSystem doc: 'fx never reads ctx.camera on the CPU for orientation or placement: billboards expand in view space in the vertex shader; the weather volume wraps around the built-in cameraPosition uniform. GPU buffers are written at most once per rendered frame, from the batch mesh onBeforeRender (or when ctx.time.substep === ctx.time.substeps - 1).' `TimeState.readonly substep: number; readonly substeps: number;` (index and count of the current frame's substeps, set by core in time.advance).

gaps.area: performance - option objects, pool capacities, quality changes
gaps.problem: spawn/tracer/beam/telegraph/damageNumber/play/playAt/loop all take optional option objects; callers will write `{ normal, dir }` literals in hot paths (9 pellets x impact + decal + sound per blast), which is per-frame garbage the brief forbids, and the contract does not say the callee copies them. Pool sizes that gameplay depends on are unstated: if telegraph() runs out during a 16-skitter arrival plus mortars, a danger zone is silently invisible. FX reads particleScale/maxDecals on 'quality:changed' and may reallocate pools mid-run.
gaps.proposedChange: Doc on FxSpawnOptions, TracerOptions, BeamOptions, TelegraphOptions, DamageNumberOptions, LightningOptions, SoundOptions, LoopOptions: 'read during the call and never retained; callers in update paths reuse module-level objects.' core/make.ts adds `makeFxOptions(): FxSpawnOptions`, `clearFxOptions(o: FxSpawnOptions): FxSpawnOptions`, `makeSoundOptions(): SoundOptions`. core/constants.ts: `export const FX_CAPS = { particles: 4000, telegraphs: 96, beams: 32, trails: 96, bolts: 24, damageNumbers: 64, tracers: 128 } as const; export const MAX_PROJECTILES = 96;` with 'telegraph() and persistent beam() never fail below these caps; beyond them the oldest timed one is recycled'. FxSystem doc: 'all pools are allocated for the ultra caps in init(); quality:changed only changes caps, never allocates or disposes.'

gaps.area: settings
gaps.problem: (1) settings.ts set() (68-74) writes localStorage synchronously on every call; a slider drag is 60 JSON.stringify + setItem per second. (2) There is no brightness control, the standard remedy for Stormnight/Eclipse on dim phone or laptop panels. (3) reduceFlashes defaults to false even when the OS asks for reduced motion.
gaps.proposedChange: settings.ts: emit 'settings:changed' immediately but persist on a 300 ms trailing timer, flushed on visibilitychange (hidden) and pagehide. `SettingsData.brightness: number` ('0.7 .. 1.4, default 1. Applied by RENDER as a final exposure multiplier'; SETTING_RANGES.brightness = [0.7, 1.4]). When no stored value exists: `reduceFlashes = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`.

gaps.area: core/input.ts + platform - smaller robustness items
gaps.problem: (a) device starts as 'keyboardMouse' on phones, so the first menu frame shows keyboard glyphs until a touch (Playwright touch emulation reports pointer: coarse, any-pointer: fine false). (b) In free look requestCapture sets cursor 'crosshair' (line 619), which reads as the aim point although shots go to the screen centre; and the canvas click that only re-acquires a lost lock also fires the weapon. (c) Pointer lock is requested without unadjustedMovement, so OS mouse acceleration distorts aim. (d) A mouseup lost outside the frame leaves fire held (only blur releases it). (e) Input.rumble has no assigned caller. (f) Touch UI and the bot share one virtual channel: a touch layer that calls clearVirtual() or writes setVirtualMove every frame cancels the bot, and virtual buttons stay held when the touch layer is hidden mid-press. (g) Fullscreen has no stated owner.
gaps.proposedChange: (a) `let device: InputDevice = matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches && !matchMedia('(any-pointer: fine)').matches ? 'touch' : 'keyboardMouse';`. (b) free look uses cursor 'default'; in onMouseDown `if (!locked && everLocked && !lockDisabled) { tryLock(true); return; }` (that click does not fire). (c) try `canvas.requestPointerLock({ unadjustedMovement: true })`, on NotSupportedError retry without options. (d) in onMouseMove: `if (e.buttons === 0 && heldButtons.size > 0) releaseHeldMouse();`. (e) Doc: 'PLAYER rumbles on damage taken (0.3 + amount / 60, 0.15 s) and hard landings; WEAPONS per shot (def.shake * 1.5, 0.06 s); COMBAT for explosions within 12 m of the player.' (f) UiSystem doc: 'touch controls call setVirtualMove / setVirtualButton only from pointer events, release exactly the buttons they hold and zero their stick whenever they hide (mode !== playing, wantsPointer(), device change, pointercancel), and never call clearVirtual().' (g) 'Fullscreen is UI-only: show the button only when document.fullscreenEnabled; call document.documentElement.requestFullscreen() inside the click handler with .catch(() => {}).'

gaps.area: over-engineering and small enum fixes
gaps.problem: Presentation-side surface with no user or with two ways to do one thing: BeamKind 'tether' (no user) and 'chain' (chain lightning can also be fx.lightningBolt or FxId 'chainArc' - three implementations of one visual); TrailKind 'supply' next to FxId 'supplyTrail'; TrailKind 'dash' (first person: never visible; the dash look is post.dashBlur + 'dashBurst'); SoundId 'heartbeat' next to LoopId 'heartbeatLoop'; RenderSystem.renderer is public, inviting other systems to call compile/setRenderTarget; RenderStats.drawCalls has no definition of what it counts. Missing UI sounds for moments the UI owns.
gaps.proposedChange: Delete BeamKind 'tether' and 'chain' (doc: 'chain lightning = fx.lightningBolt(from, to, { color: PALETTE.player, branches: 1, light: false }) + spawn("chainArc") at each victim'); delete FxId 'supplyTrail' (keep TrailKind 'supply'); delete TrailKind 'dash'; delete SoundId 'heartbeat'. RenderSystem.renderer doc: 'for render itself and tests; no other system calls methods on it or reads capabilities'. RenderStats.drawCalls doc: 'all passes of the last frame including shadow and post'. Add SoundIds for UI-owned moments: 'uiStartRun', 'uiGradeReveal', 'uiStatTick' (the stats count-up; replaces director 'scoreTick').

overallAssessment:
No blockers for world, render, fx, audio, ui, input or the harness: each can be built against `src/core/types.ts` as it stands. FxId, SoundId, LoopId, DecalKind and TrailKind cover everything these systems must render or play and everything gameplay will call; only three UI sounds are missing. The risk is in the seams, with 21 major and 16 minor findings. Nothing in the repo was edited.

**Assignment docs contradict the contract** (both sides would ship the feature):
- Ambient lightning and thunder: `assign/render.md` gives them to render, `types.ts` to fx weather.
- The "low" preset: `render.md` says no composer, while `types.ts` says the frame is always HDR. This decides whether every custom shader in world, fx, enemies and weapons looks right.
- Reduce-flashes: `fx.md` has fx tame flashes, `types.ts` says only render does.
- The fatal panel: `ui.md` lists it, the contract forbids the UI to build one.
- Pipe racks: `world.md` makes them visual-only at 4 m, inside the wasp flight band of 4–9 m.

**Two-sided ambiguities** (each team will guess differently):
- Whether an fx id is a one-shot burst or a stream the caller re-spawns, and how blast radius maps to visual size.
- The unit of `lightFlash` intensity, and how to keep a light on a moving object.
- Whether pooled handles can be reissued, so a stale handle stops another owner's beam or loop.
- Draw order of transparent objects across five systems.
- How `SettingsData.quality` can hold an automatic default without overwriting the user's choice.
- Enter and arrow keys firing both the native control and the `ui*` action.
- Whether jump-pad arcs survive the player's air-speed clamp.

**Lifecycle holes:**
- Loops started in `init()` are dead (audio is locked), and loops started in `reset()` by world, render or fx are killed by `audio.reset()` later in the same pass. World ambience can never sound as written.
- The same `stopAll` cuts the UI click that triggered `startRun` or `toMenu`.
- fx and audio miss the initial time of day because the event only fires on change.
- One-shot sounds cannot be stopped when their attacker dies.

**Time scale:** audio must follow only the overclock and slowmo requests, otherwise every hit-stop dives the pitch to 5 %. The player's own muzzle flashes and tracers run at 0.4x during Overclock.

**Real bugs in core:**
- `game.ts`: the failure streak is only cleared for update, lateUpdate and render, so three failures ever of any reset, mode-change, unlock or resize call are fatal. `unlock:audio` runs on every click, so a device that cannot create an AudioContext dies after three clicks.
- `game.ts`: boot never yields to paint, and resize wipes the frame that was just drawn.
- `input.ts`: pointer lock is permanently disabled after gamepad or non-gesture starts.
- `input.ts`: non-standard gamepads cause drift and per-frame device flapping.
- `input.ts`: trackpad scrolling cycles weapons on every wheel event.
- `input.ts`: arrow keys on a focused button scroll the host page.
- `index.html`: the Google Fonts stylesheet blocks first paint and the module script.

**Harness:** it only ever runs top-level with `?test=1`, so the sandboxed, query-less shipping form is untested. The proposed fix is a `window.name` switch for test mode plus a sandbox embed mode with a CORS header.

**Checked by running probes against `dist`:**
- In `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` the build does not load at all: the module script is blocked by CORS from the opaque origin.
- In the same frame localStorage and pointer lock throw SecurityError, fullscreen is disabled, an AudioContext created without activation stays suspended, and `window.name` set by the host is readable.
- Five ArrowDown presses on a focused button inside the frame scrolled the host page 200 px.
- Headless Chromium has WebGL2 with half-float targets on SwiftShader.

The other input and core bugs were found by reading the code, not by running it.
